title: Chapter 13 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of CSS transitions, transforms, 3D, keyframes, and animation best practices!

questions.question: Which CSS property allows you to smoothly change from one style to another over time?
questions.explanation: `transition` defines a smooth change between two states.

questions.question: Where should you place the `transition` property to ensure it works both on hover and when returning?
questions.explanation: Placing it on the element's normal state makes it transition in both directions.

questions.question: The `transition` shorthand property takes values in the order: property, duration, timing-function, ______.
questions.explanation: The order is `<property> <duration> <timing-function> <delay>`.

questions.question: Which of the following properties is recommended for performant animations?
questions.explanation: `transform` and `opacity` only trigger compositing, avoiding layout/paint.

questions.question: What does `transform: translateX(100px)` do?
options: Moves the element 100px to the left
Moves the element 100px to the right
questions.explanation: `translateX` moves the element horizontally; positive values move right.

questions.question: How do you rotate an element by 45 degrees clockwise?
questions.explanation: `rotate()` takes an angle, with positive values rotating clockwise.

questions.question: What is the default `transform-origin`?
questions.explanation: The default pivot point is the centre of the element (50% 50%).

questions.question: To enable 3D rendering for children of a transformed parent, which property is required?
questions.explanation: `transform-style: preserve-3d;` allows children to exist in the parent's 3D space.

questions.question: What does `perspective: 800px;` on a container do?
options: Sets the width of the container
Defines the distance between the viewer and the screen, affecting 3D depth
questions.explanation: `perspective` gives a 3D‑space to child elements; smaller values produce stronger perspective.

questions.question: `backface-visibility: hidden;` hides the front face of an element.
questions.explanation: It hides the **back** face when the element is rotated away from the viewer.

questions.question: The `@keyframes` rule defines:
options: The timing function for a transition
The steps of an animation at specific percentages
The start and end of a transition
questions.explanation: `@keyframes` specifies the intermediate waypoints of an animation.

questions.question: Which property makes an animation loop forever?
questions.explanation: `animation-iteration-count: infinite;` repeats the animation indefinitely.

questions.question: What does `animation-direction: alternate;` do?
options: Plays the animation in reverse only
Plays the animation forward then backwards on even iterations
Stops the animation after one cycle
questions.explanation: `alternate` makes the animation play normally on odd cycles and in reverse on even cycles.

questions.question: `animation-fill-mode: forwards;` will:
options: Keep the element hidden before the animation
Retain the styles of the last keyframe after the animation ends
questions.explanation: `forwards` applies the styles of the final keyframe after the animation completes.

questions.question: You can use `animation-play-state: paused;` to pause an animation on hover.
questions.explanation: Yes, it toggles the running state, often used with `:hover` to pause a running animation.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best way to animate a button's hover lift effect for performance?
questions.explanation: `transform: translateY()` is composited and doesn't trigger layout.

questions.question: What does `will-change: transform;` do?
options: Forces the element to be invisible
Hints the browser to optimise for upcoming transform changes
questions.explanation: It tells the browser to prepare a GPU layer for potential animation, improving performance.

questions.question: How should you respect users who have enabled 'reduce motion' in their OS?
options: Ignore it, animations are too important
Use `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` to disable or simplify animations
questions.explanation: The `prefers-reduced-motion` media query lets you provide a reduced‑motion experience.

questions.question: When using `transition: all 0.3s;`, what is a potential downside?
options: It may animate properties that don't need to change, causing performance issues
questions.explanation: `all` can trigger unnecessary layout calculations, even for properties you didn't intend to animate.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid `animation-timing-function` value?
questions.explanation: `bounce` is not a built‑in keyword. You must create it via `cubic-bezier()` or keyframes.

questions.question: What is the keyframe syntax to start an animation at 50% opacity and end fully opaque?
questions.explanation: Option D correctly uses percentage selectors from 0% to 100%.

questions.question: CSS animations can run without any user interaction.
questions.explanation: Unlike transitions, animations can start automatically on page load.

questions.question: You want an element to rotate continuously and stop when hovered. Which technique works?
options: Remove the animation class with JavaScript
questions.explanation: `animation-play-state: paused;` on hover will freeze the animation.
